verses.zh: 摩西立完了帐幕，就把帐幕用膏抹了，使它成圣，又把其中的器具和坛，并坛上的器具，都抹了，使它成圣。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] When Moses had completed setting up the tabernacle,[NOTE:2] he anointed it and consecrated it and all its furnishings, and he anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils.
notes: This long and repetitious chapter has several parts to it: the introduction (vv. 1-3), the assigning of gifts (vv. 4-9), the time of presentation (vv. 10-11), and then the tribes (vv. 12-83), and then a summary (vv. 84-89).

This chapter belongs chronologically after Lev 8:11 because Aaron and his sons were not yet made the celebrants and officiants of the new shrine (completed in Exodus). Here then chapters 7-9 are actually earlier than chapters 1-6, and form a supplement by adding information not found in Exodus and Leviticus. The first verse here recapitulates the first act of Moses in consecrating the shrine (Exod 30:23-31).tn The construction of this line begins with the temporal indicator (traditionally translated “and it came to pass”) and then after the idiomatic “in the day of” (= “when”) uses the Piel infinitive construct from כָּלָה (kalah). The infinitive is governed by the subjective genitive, “Moses,” the formal subject of the clause. The object of the infinitive is the second infinitive, “to set up” (לְהָקִים, lehaqim). This infinitive, the Hiphil, serves as the direct object, answering the question of what it was that Moses completed. The entire clause is an adverbial clause of time.

verses.zh: 当天，以色列的众首领，就是各族的族长，都来奉献。他们是各支派的首领，管理那些被数的人。
verses.en: Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their clans,[NOTE:1] made an offering. They were the leaders of the tribes; they were the ones who had been supervising[NOTE:2] the numbering.
notes: Heb “the house of their fathers.”

The form is the Qal active participle from the verb “to stand” (עָמַד, ʿamad). The form describes these leaders as “the ones standing over [the ones numbered].” The expression, along with the clear indication of the first census in chapter 1, shows that this was a supervisory capacity.

verses.zh: 他们把自己的供物送到耶和华面前，就是六辆篷子车和十二只公牛。每两个首领奉献一辆车，每首领奉献一只牛。他们把这些都奉到帐幕前。
verses.en: They brought[NOTE:1] their offerings before the Lord, six covered carts[NOTE:2] and twelve oxen—one cart for every two of the leaders, and an ox for each one; and they presented them in front of the tabernacle.
notes: Heb “and they brought.”
For a discussion and drawings, see W. S. McCullough, IDB 1:540. But see also D. J. Wiseman, IBD 1:254.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你要收下这些，好作会幕的使用，都要照利未人所办的事交给他们。」
verses.en: “Receive these gifts[NOTE:1] from them, that they may be[NOTE:2] used in doing the work[NOTE:3] of the tent of meeting; and you must give them to the Levites, to every man[NOTE:4] as his service requires.”[NOTE:5]
notes: The object is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied.

The verb is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive; following the imperative, this could be given an independent volitive translation (“they shall be”), but more fittingly a subordinated translation expressing the purpose of receiving the gifts.
The sentence uses the infinitive construct expressing purpose, followed by its cognate accusative: “[that they may be] for doing the work of” (literally, “serving the service of”).
The noun אִישׁ (ʾish) is in apposition to the word “Levites,” and is to be taken in a distributive sense: “to the Levites, [to each] man according to his service.”
The expression כְּפִי (kefi) is “according to the mouth of.” Here, it would say “according to the mouth of his service,” which would mean “what his service calls for.”

verses.zh: 于是摩西收了车和牛，交给利未人，
verses.en: So Moses accepted the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.

verses.zh: 把两辆车，四只牛，照革顺子孙所办的事交给他们，
verses.en: He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their service required;

verses.zh: 又把四辆车，八只牛，照米拉利子孙所办的事交给他们；他们都在祭司亚伦的儿子以他玛手下。
verses.en: and he gave four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their service required, under the authority[NOTE:1] of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 但车与牛都没有交给哥辖子孙；因为他们办的是圣所的事，在肩头上抬圣物。
verses.en: But to the Kohathites he gave none, because the service of the holy things, which they carried[NOTE:1] on their shoulders, was their responsibility.[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb is the imperfect tense, but it describes their customary activity—they had to carry, they used to carry.
Heb “upon them,” meaning “their duty.”

verses.zh: 用膏抹坛的日子，首领都来行奉献坛的礼，众首领就在坛前献供物。
verses.en: The leaders offered[NOTE:1] gifts[NOTE:2] for[NOTE:3] the dedication[NOTE:4] of the altar when it was anointed.[NOTE:5] And the leaders presented[NOTE:6] their offering before the altar.
notes: The verse begins with the preterite and vav (ו) consecutive: “and they offered.”
The direct object, “gifts,” is implied but not actually stated in the Hebrew text. It has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons and for clarity.
The sign of the accusative here must indicate an adverbial accusative and not the direct object; they offered their gifts for the dedication of the altar.

Some commentators take the word “dedication” in the sense of a dedication gift, and so make it the direct object. Many modern scholars assume that this is a late word, belonging only in P, the Chronicler, and the heading of Ps 30 (a Davidic psalm).
The adverbial clause uses the Niphal infinitive construct as the main verb. The word is the well-known מָשַׁח (mashakh, “to anoint, smear”).
Heb “offered,” but this is redundant and has been translated as “presented” for stylistic reasons. The same phrase occurs in vv. 11 and 12.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「众首领为行奉献坛的礼，要每天一个首领来献供物。」
verses.en: For the Lord said to Moses, “They must present their offering, one leader for each day,[NOTE:1] for the dedication of the altar.”
notes: The distributive sense is achieved by repetition: “one leader for the day, one leader for the day.”

verses.zh: 头一日献供物的是犹大支派的亚米拿达的儿子拿顺。
verses.en: The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: The tribe of Judah is listed first. It seems that it had already achieved a place of prominence based on the patriarchal promise of the Messiahship in Judah (Gen 49:10).

verses.zh: 他的供物是：一个银盘子，重一百三十舍客勒，一个银碗，重七十舍客勒，都是按圣所的平，也都盛满了调油的细面作素祭；
verses.en: His offering was one silver platter weighing 130 shekels,[NOTE:1] and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing 70 shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each of them full of fine flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;
notes: The word “shekels” has been supplied in the translation for clarity. So also in vv. 19, 20, 25, 26, 31, 32, 37, 38, 43, 44, 49, 50, 55, 56, 60, 62, 66, 68, 73, 74, 79, 85, 86.

verses.zh: 一个金盂，重十舍客勒，盛满了香；
verses.en: one gold pan weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;

verses.zh: 一只公牛犊，一只公绵羊，一只一岁的公羊羔作燔祭；
verses.en: one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb in its first year, for a burnt offering;

verses.zh: 一只公山羊作赎罪祭；
verses.en: one male goat for a purification offering;

verses.zh: 两只公牛，五只公绵羊，五只公山羊，五只一岁的公羊羔作平安祭。这是亚米拿达儿子拿顺的供物。
verses.en: and for the sacrifice of peace offerings: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

verses.zh: 第二日来献的是以萨迦子孙的首领、苏押的儿子拿坦业。
verses.en: On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of Issachar, presented an offering.

verses.zh: 一只公牛犊，一只公绵羊，一只一岁的公羊羔作燔祭；
verses.en: one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb in its first year, for a burnt offering;

verses.zh: 一只公山羊作赎罪祭；
verses.en: one male goat for a purification offering;

verses.zh: 两只公牛，五只公绵羊，五只公山羊，五只一岁的公羊羔作平安祭。这是以南儿子亚希拉的供物。
verses.en: and for the sacrifice of peace offerings: two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five lambs in their first year. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.

verses.zh: 用膏抹坛的日子，以色列的众首领为行献坛之礼所献的是：银盘子十二个，银碗十二个，金盂十二个；
verses.en: This was the dedication for the altar from the leaders of Israel, when it was anointed: twelve silver platters, twelve silver sprinkling bowls, and twelve gold pans.

verses.zh: 每盘子重一百三十舍客勒，每碗重七十舍客勒。一切器皿的银子，按圣所的平，共有二千四百舍客勒。
verses.en: Each silver platter weighed 130 shekels, and each silver sprinkling bowl weighed 70 shekels. All the silver of the vessels weighed 2,400 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

verses.zh: 十二个金盂盛满了香，按圣所的平，每盂重十舍客勒，所有的金子共一百二十舍客勒。
verses.en: The twelve gold pans full of incense weighed 10 shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel; all the gold of the pans weighed 120 shekels.

verses.zh: 作燔祭的，共有公牛十二只，公羊十二只，一岁的公羊羔十二只，并同献的素祭作赎罪祭的公山羊十二只；
verses.en: All the animals for the burnt offering were 12 young bulls, 12 rams, 12 male lambs in their first year, with their grain offering, and 12 male goats for a purification offering.

verses.zh: 作平安祭的，共有公牛二十四只，公绵羊六十只，公山羊六十只，一岁的公羊羔六十只。这就是用膏抹坛之后，为行奉献坛之礼所献的。
verses.en: All the animals for the sacrifice for the peace offering were 24 young bulls, 60 rams, 60 male goats, and 60 lambs in their first year. These were the dedication offerings for the altar after it was anointed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Even though the chapter seems wearisome and repetitious to the modern reader, it is a significant document. A. Rainey shows how it matches the exact ledgers of ancient sanctuaries (see ZPEB 5:202). The recording would have been done by the priestly scribes. Of the many points that can be observed here, it should not be missed that each tribe, regardless of its size or relative importance, was on equal footing before the Lord. Each tribe shared in the work of the Lord equally. Each tribe approached the sanctuary in precisely the same way on this memorable occasion. All such devotion to the work of the Lord was to receive the blessing of God.

verses.zh: 摩西进会幕要与耶和华说话的时候，听见法柜的施恩座以上、二基路伯中间有与他说话的声音，就是耶和华与他说话。
verses.en: Now when Moses went into[NOTE:1] the tent of meeting to speak with the Lord,[NOTE:2] he heard the voice speaking to him from above the atonement lid[NOTE:3] that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim.[NOTE:4] Thus he spoke to him.
notes: The adverbial clause of time is constructed with the infinitive construct of the verb “to enter” (בּוֹא, boʾ) with the preposition and with the subjective genitive that follows serving as the subject of the clause. The verse is strategic in the structure of the book: At the completion of the dedication with the offerings Moses received more revelation from the Lord in the tent. This verse therefore lays the foundation for what follows.

The MT is obscure here, simply giving the purpose infinitive and the prepositional phrase (“with him”). But the following clause using the Hitpael of the same verb, introducing a reflexive sense: “then he heard the voice speaking with him.” The Greek clarified it by inserting “Lord” after the word “voice.” The editor of BHS favors emendation of the form to a Piel participle rather than the Hitpael of the MT (reading מְדַבֵּר [medabber] instead of מִדַּבֵּר [middabber], the Hitpael with assimilation). Most commentators agree with the change, assuming there was a mistaken pointing in the MT.

The Hebrew word כַּפֹּרֶת (kapporet) has been traditionally rendered “mercy seat,” but since the ark is the footstool (see Ps 132), this translation is somewhat misleading. The word is etymologically connected to the verb “to make atonement.” A technical translation would be “place of atonement” or “propitiatory”; a more common translation would be “cover, lid”—provided that the definition “to cover” does not get transferred to the verb “to atone,” for that idea belongs to a homonym. See also Exod 25:17.

The cherubim are the carved forms of the angels attached to the ark. They indicate the guarding role of this order of angels in the holy of holies. They were also embroidered on the curtains. For basic material see ZPEB 1:788-90, and R. K. Harrison, ISBE 1:642-43.
